[[File:Tuatha'an.JPG|thumb|A female ''[[Tuatha'an]]'' dancing the ''tiganza''.]]
{{quote|Outstretched arms spread her shawl behind her; her hips undulated as her bare feet shuffled to the beat of the drums....She turned in small circles, smiling over her shoulder at him.|{{1|27}}}}

The '''''tiganza''''' is a sensual dance performed by ''[[Tuatha'an]]'' women. The dance involves shuffling steps to the slow beat of drums, small circular turns, and a slow rotation of the hips that is emphasized by the sway of a fringed shawl. It is usually done barefoot to the light of the campfire.{{ref/book|1|27}}

[[Perrin]] describes the ''tiganza'' as the Tinker women's swaying, hip-rolling dance that sets the heart pounding.{{Ref/book|4|42}}

== Parallels ==
''Tiganza'' is similar to "Tzigane", a word for the [[wikipedia:Romani people|Romani people]] who are nomadic like the ''Tuatha'an''.{{ref|[[Origins of the Wheel of Time]], ''tiganza''}} This is commonly applied to Romani music, especially of a Hungarian origin.{{ref|[https://www.dictionary.com/browse/tzigane Tzigane: Dictionary.com definition with examples]}}<ref>[https://www.oed.com/view/Entry/208474?redirectedFrom=Tzigane& Tzigane: OED (definition B)]</ref> ''Tzigane'' is also a famous piece of music by Maurice Ravel, dedicated to Hungarian violinist, Jelly d'Arányi.{{ref|[https://www.allmusic.com/composition/tzigane-rhapsodie-de-concert-for-violin-piano-or-orchestra-m-76-mc0002397565?1675083564896 Allmusic.com: Tzigane description and recording history.]}}<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EbWV7fTIooQ&ab_channel=MenuhinCompetition María Dueñas performs Ravel's Tzigane]</ref>

The rhythmic nature of the dance as well as the emphasis of the hips, however, suggest a dance closer to [[wikipedia:Belly dancing|belly dancing]]
